debug_uart.label: ST-Link VCP (USART3 — Nucleo-144 wiring, PD8/PD9 AF7)

ethernet.label: onboard 10/100 Ethernet: ETH MAC + LAN8742A PHY (RMII, addr 0, RJ45 CN14). PHY nRST is tied to the board NRST net on MB1137 — there is NO dedicated GPIO PHY reset; reset_pin=PG2 is an unused placeholder to satisfy the driver's reset-pin requirement (the driver also soft-resets the PHY via BMCR.RESET over MDIO, which is the reset that actually matters here).

adc.label: ADC1 — external channels only; this part's chip data carries no internal-channel map

bridge.label: TIM1 complementary bridge on the ZIO header — HEADER EXPECTATION, NOT A FITTED POWER STAGE, AND NOT COMPATIBLE WITH THIS BOARD'S ETHERNET. No inverter is on a Nucleo; what this claims is that the seven pads route to TIM1, which they do. Two of them are already spoken for and the first is the one that matters: al=PB13 is RMII_TXD1 in this chip's own pin bank, so opening the bridge and the onboard PHY in one program muxes one pad twice and the Ethernet stops working. That is not a pin choice I can fix — CH1N's only two routes in this package are PA7 and PB13 and BOTH are RMII, so a three-phase complementary bridge and the PHY are mutually exclusive here, full stop. bl=PB14 is LD3 (red), which costs nothing but is not 'free' either. board-validate now says so out loud. The dead time is what an IR2110-class gate driver wants and is a PLACEHOLDER until a real board states its own. Nothing here has driven a transistor.
